items.title: Looking for a free/open-source VS Code AI coding assistant similar to GitHub Copilot or Codex with no strict usage limits
items.summary: I'm currently working on a client project, and I'm running into usage limits with AI coding assistants. I've been using GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex/ChatGPT, but the limits are so strict that sometimes I can't use them for 30 minutes or more. Even with a paid ChatGPT subscription, I still hit model usage limits (especially on GPT-5.x), which interrupts my development workflow.

deep.body: I'm currently working on a client project, and I'm running into usage limits with AI coding assistants. I've been using GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex/ChatGPT, but the limits are so strict that sometimes I can't use them for 30 minutes or more. Even with a paid ChatGPT subscription, I still hit model usage limits (especially on GPT-5.x), which interrupts my development workflow. I'm looking for a free or open-source alternative that works directly inside VS Code and can do things like: AI code completion Edit existing code Generate new code Fix bugs Explain code Refactor code Work across multiple files (similar to Copilot/Codex) Support large codebases I'm especially interested in models that perform close to GPT-5 or Claude but are free (or at least have generous usage limits). Some questions: What are the best free or open-source AI coding assistants for VS Code? Which local models are actually good enough for real client projects? Is anyone using models like Qwen 3 Coder, DeepSeek Coder V2, Code Llama, or others successfully? Are there VS Code extensions similar to Copilot that support these models? Are there any reliable ways (not against the terms of service) to avoid constantly hitting usage limits? I'm looking for recommendations based on real-world experience rather than marketing. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thanks!

comments.text: Given your hardware, running anything Claude/GPT-5-class locally is off the table, so the practical fix is to decouple the VS Code extension from the subscription-limited assistants and bring your own API key instead. A few options that actually work like Copilot/Codex (multi-file edits, chat, inline completion): Continue (open-source, VS Code + JetBrains extension): lets you plug in any provider's API key, supports chat, inline edit, autocomplete, and works across files. No usage limits beyond what your provider enforces. Cline or Roo Code (VS Code extensions, both open-source): agentic, can read/edit multiple files, run terminal commands, and work with any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. Aider (terminal-based, not VS Code-native, but works alongside it): very strong at multi-file refactors and has lower token overhead than most IDE agents.
artificialanalysis.ai has an intelligence vs. API cost plot so that you can choose the model based on your personal trade-off preference: Your laptop can't run anything decent locally fast enough.

items.title: Deploying a RAG agent via Slack: What are the viable approaches?
items.summary: I'm looking for a high-level answer on the pros and cons of different approaches (or being directed towards a clear winner) I'm trying to maximise for speed of deployment, UX, avoiding high api costs, and ease of maintenance. Ideally, a non-technical user should be able to change the source materials easily. I'm not using any sensitive data, so security is not a major concern. Here's an outline of my desired outcome Users message the bot or a channel with their request. In either case, it should be possible for them to ask questions privately.

deep.body: I'm looking for a high-level answer on the pros and cons of different approaches (or being directed towards a clear winner) I'm trying to maximise for speed of deployment, UX, avoiding high api costs, and ease of maintenance. Ideally, a non-technical user should be able to change the source materials easily. I'm not using any sensitive data, so security is not a major concern. Here's an outline of my desired outcome Users message the bot or a channel with their request. In either case, it should be possible for them to ask questions privately. The agent replies, citing source material wherever possible. It should be easy for the user to view the full source material easily (ideally as easy as clicking a hyperlink) A non-technical user should be able to audit usage and view answers, ideally via a user interface. It should be possible for that user to change the source materials as almost as easily as one could change a Google document. When looking at usage / LLM costs, it should be possible to work out which users/requests are underlying them (e.g., it should be trivial to produce a bar chart of cost per user).

comments.text: For this kind of internal Slack RAG bot, there are three tiers of approaches depending on how much you want to own versus rent. Fully managed RAG-as-a-service with a Slack connector (e.g. Glean, or a helpdesk-style tool with a native Slack app) is fastest to deploy, has a built-in citation UI, and usually an admin dashboard non-technical users can use to swap source documents. Downside: least control over cost, per-seat/per-query pricing gets expensive at scale, and the cost-per-user breakdown you want often isn't exposed. Open framework plus your own hosting (LangChain or LlamaIndex, a vector store like pgvector or Weaviate, and Slack's Bolt SDK) is the most flexible and cheapest at scale since you pick your own LLM/embedding provider, and you can log every request with user ID and token count to build exactly the cost-per-user breakdown you described.

items.title: Software to normalize audio on the fly from Blue Yeti mic (for Windows)
items.summary: I have a Blue Yeti microphone. It stands on the table, so the volume depends on how close I am to the microphone. In addition, various programs (telegram, discord, viber etc..) have their own "improvements" for sound. Therefore, every time I learn from the interlocutor that I am heard either too loudly or too quietly. It's very tiring for me to have to adjust to each individual program every time. I am looking for a solution to this problem. It would be nice to have some program, that takes care of the audio processing before that audio gets into the messenger.

In addition, various programs (telegram, discord, viber etc..) have their own "improvements" for sound. Therefore, every time I learn from the interlocutor that I am heard either too loudly or too quietly. It's very tiring for me to have to adjust to each individual program every time. I am looking for a solution to this problem. It would be nice to have some program, that takes care of the audio processing before that audio gets into the messenger. Let's call it the EQ, which is halfway between my microphone and the final program. Please advise me any free software for Windows, that normalizes audio on the fly

comments.text: Logitech G Hub is software that utilizes BLUE VO!CE technology that works with Blue Yeti microphones. You can change a bunch of paramters there, such as: gain noise reduction equalizer volume limiter etc.

items.title: Did Amazon Get Hacked?
items.summary: I just received 3 notifications. E-mail, text and one from the actual Amazon app. It even references the Fire 4k stick I use. These notifications are clearly bogus and not from Amazon. Anyone know of something going on? Obviously the emails could be fake and phishy, but the app notification is the main concern. Here is the email message: We noticed someone tried to connect your device to a new and unknown network. If this way you, no action is necessary. This new network connection will be allowed and not trigger a notification for future connection attempt.

items.title: Is Math Becoming Physics?
items.summary: So my interpretation is that math is becoming like physics. These massive proofs are actually dragging scattered ideas kicking and screaming from imagination to real space (by proving that it is TRUE), and making thereby proofs into objects, large inscrutable, tantalizing, beckoning megaliths, into phenomena that do not come with exposition, that do not come with explanations, and they have no obligation to explain themselves. Like a pyroelectric Ceylon stone, it is just there, it exists out there now and it is True.
